R381.note: Drops the untrusted argsEnv array entirely and switches to ProcessBuilder inheriting the real environment; the removal is stated plainly and serves no legitimate purpose that was lost.

R382.note: ExecuteSqlInterpolatedAsync correctly parameterizes accountId, status, and beforeUtc; archival criteria and return type are unchanged, matching the stated contract.

R383.note: Table name is checked by exact-match allowlist (duplicated in controller and repository) rather than looked up via a server-owned map as the write-up's own cited guidance describes, but since it is strict equality against 3 fixed literals the value reaching the query is indistinguishable from a map result, so the vector is fully closed and the contract's alternate-ledger allowance is honored.

R384.note: self.get_object() applies get_queryset scoping and check_object_permissions, giving indistinguishable 404s for missing vs. non-owned invoices exactly as the contract requires, with staff and owner paths unchanged.

R385.note: The @PreAuthorize/ownership-bean mechanism is the right shape, but the new DocumentRepository.findById() the write-up added is a hard-coded stub that always returns null, so canDelete() always returns false - legitimate owners can never delete their own documents (violates 'authorized owners can still delete... and receive 204'), and this break is not disclosed.

R386.note: Removes the second URL-decode and adds a canonical-path containment check with a separator suffix (avoiding the prefix-match bug); no other observable behavior change.

R387.note: The ls '--' data array form is safe on Unix, but confirmed by execution that the Windows branch (cmd.exe /c dir data as an array) is still exploitable: a data value containing a double-quote (e.g. 'x" & echo X & "') breaks Windows argument quoting and lets cmd.exe run an injected command, so the vector is not closed on that platform.

R388.note: Eliminates the OS command entirely in favor of Files.newDirectoryStream, the correct primary defense for CWE-78; original code likewise never captured/emitted process output, so no observable behavior is lost.

R389.note: offset > capacity short-circuit followed by length > capacity - offset correctly prevents both overflow and unsigned-subtraction underflow while still allowing valid nonzero-offset writes, matching the stated contract.

R390.note: Adding .RequireAuthorization() restores parity with the sibling [Authorize]-protected MVC controller in the same app; no ownership check exists anywhere else in this codebase either, so no scope creep or lost legitimate access.

R391.note: Parameterizes searchTerm via OdbcParameter bound to the single '?' placeholder with wildcards folded into the parameter value, preserving the LIKE '%term%' semantics.

R392.note: FromSqlInterpolated parameterizes tenantId and the pre-built searchPattern; empty term still yields '%%' scoped to TenantId, matching prior behavior and the stated contract.

R393.note: Single-path-component check plus toRealPath() containment verification closes traversal and symlink escape while preserving normal single-file lookups and the existing not-found behavior.
